audit.whatIsWrong: Stored chart read Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Skill/Skill in both layers. The packet levelChart is Garen/Garen/Sett/Sett/Sett/Garen/Skill. Four rows disagree, and the page's own whys[] already contradicted the chart: whys[0] says 'You out-damage early Sett at level 1' and whys[5] says 'Post-6 your Q-silence and Perseverance retake the lane', both while the chart handed those stages to Sett.
audit.why: Sett has no ability at level 1 that beats Garen's Q auto-reset plus silence, and Haymaker is not yet ranked. His window opens at 3-5 once Haymaker banks grit and Facebreaker is online, and closes again at the first item where Perseverance out-sustains a no-lifesteal frame. Difficulty stays EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 51.21% win rate.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Garen, Garen, Sett, Sett, Sett, Garen, Skill in both layers, proposed as one atomic group.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly placed: Sett's 3-5 grit window, his Level 6 R, Garen's first-item sustain retake, and the even late duel. Only the ability naming inside them needed fixing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated Facebreaker as an unconditional stun and told the player to bait it. Riot's text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Against a solo Garen with nothing behind him, Facebreaker is a slow, not a stun — and Garen's Q explicitly breaks free of all slows. Haymaker's cooldown was given as 16s; Riot's value is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, so 18s at rank 1. The R was written as 'Show Stopper'; the real name is The Show Stopper (packet flagged this, distance 4).
audit.why: This flips the whole trading rule. The player was being told to fear a stun he can usually prevent by positioning, and to bait a cooldown whose real length he was never given. The actual punishable window is Haymaker at 18s rank 1 combined with an empty grit bar, and the way to disarm Facebreaker is to fight clear of minions rather than to bait it.
audit.corrected: State the two-sided condition on Facebreaker, the Q slow-purge answer to the one-sided version, Haymaker's true 18s rank-1 cooldown, and the correct ability name The Show Stopper.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice did not tie Judgment ticks to the grit bar Haymaker spends.
audit.why: Haymaker passively stores the damage Sett takes as Grit, so an uncommitted Judgment spin is literally loading his counter-punch. The trade rule is to spend E after his W is gone, not before.
audit.corrected: Sequencing keyed to the grit bar being empty.

notes: Two things to know. First, the level chart was wrong in four of seven rows against the packet and against the page's own whys[] text; it is proposed as one atomic group. Second, Facebreaker was described everywhere as a stun to bait — it only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett, so a solo Garen with no minion behind him takes a slow, which Decisive Strike purges outright. That changes the positioning advice, not just the wording. The R was also mis-named 'Show Stopper' in four places (real name: The Show Stopper), which the packet had flagged. UNVERIFIED and left alone: the kit's derived 'grounding' flag on The Show Stopper and the page's claim that it suppresses — neither appears in Riot's description, so no text asserts either now.
